messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am a newer to Cardinal and R. This is probably more like a R question.
I am trying to plot the example data using image function. I noticed in a few cases that I can adjust the window size to change the position of legend in the plot to make the image pretty. But in some cases this method fails. I am wondering how do you solve this in the plot that you show in the cardinal manual.
Thanks,
Jian

messages.subject: Re: Legend position in plotted images of cardinal example data
messages.subject_clean: Legend position in plotted images of cardinal example data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jian,

Thank you for using Cardinal! Yes, using R's base graphics, adjusting the window size after plotting will move the legend around a bit, but there is no standard behavior for this.

Right now, there are no options in Cardinal for customizing the size or placement of the automatically-generated legends.

However, you can still make some adjustments by changing the canvas size when outputting the plots to files (pdf, jpeg, png, etc.). In the vignettes, all of the plots are output to pdf behind-the-scenes, which is why they may appear slightly different than the default interactive R graphics.

You can try, for example:

pdf(file="myplot.pdf", height=6, width=6)
## insert image() or plot() commands here
dev.off()

and adjusting the height and width until you get desired results.

In the future, I may try adding more options for customizing the legends, but hopefully this suggestion helps for now!

-Kyle

messages.subject: Re: Error importing data
messages.body_plain:
> Hi Kyle,
> I used the following code:
> >name<-"29oxa3150_1000"
> > folder<-"C:\ Users\ Xin\ Desktop\ 29oxa3"
> > data<-readAnalyze(name, folder)
> The error is :"Error: readAnalyze: C:\ Users\ Xin\ Desktop\ 29oxa3\29oxa3150_1000.hdr does not exist."
> Is there anything wrong? Thanks a lot!
> -Xin

Hi Xin,

I expect the problem is the Windows-style "\" directory separators.

R expects either Unix-style separators "/", or you need to escape the "\" by using "\\".

Try either "C:\\Users\\Xin\\Desktop\\29oxa3" or "C:/Users/Xin/Desktop/29oxa3".

Also try "list.files(folder)" and see if you can see your files. If you can't, there is some problem with how you are typing the path to the folder.

-Kyle
